### workspace binding --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace binding set [WORKSPACE] [--pane PANE] --kind run|review|play --id ID [--step STEP] [--attempt N] [--focus TEXT] [--instructions PATH] [--artifacts PATH] [--pack NAME]... [--name NAME] [--json]
       workspace binding show [--pane %ID] [--json]
       workspace binding clear [--pane %ID] [--json]

Bind a tmux pane to a workflow run, a PR review or a library play. When the agent
in a bound pane starts a session (startup, /clear, resume or compact), session-event
reminds it of its subject, so it survives a lost context. Nothing is typed into the pane.

A pane is stored by its tmux pane id (%19) and only counts in the tmux session it
was bound in. set takes a pane id or window.pane of the workspace's own session;
show and clear take a pane id. All three default to $TMUX_PANE, the pane the
command runs in. WORKSPACE (or --name) defaults to the project detected from the
current directory. start --play and launch --play bind the pane they sent a play
to (kind play). show marks a binding stale when the pane is no longer in the tmux
session and slot it was bound in; a stale binding is not announced.

--pack lists library packs (see `workspace instructions --help`) the hook also prints, so
they survive /clear and compaction. start and launch set it for the packs they send;
a pane sent packs but no play is bound with kind play and id play/<first pack>. Setting
a binding replaces the whole earlier one, its packs included.

        --name NAME                  Workspace name (set)
        --pane PANE                  Pane id (%19) or, for set, window.pane (0.1)
        --kind KIND                  run, review or play (set)
        --id ID                      Run id, review id such as acme/api#835, or play/NAME (set)
        --step STEP                  Step name (set)
        --attempt N                  Step attempt, 1 or more (set)
        --focus TEXT                 Review focus, e.g. security (set)
        --instructions PATH          File holding the pane's instructions (set); stored as an absolute path
        --artifacts PATH             Directory holding the subject's artifacts (set); stored as an absolute path
        --pack NAME                  Library pack the agent is also reminded of (set; repeatable; replaces the stored list)
        --json                       Print one JSON action document
    -h, --help                       Show this help

Examples:
  workspace binding set --kind play --id play/orchestrator    # from inside the agent's own pane: remind it of a play after a /clear
  workspace binding show    # from inside an agent's pane: what it is reminded of after a /clear
  workspace binding clear    # from inside the agent's pane: stop reminding it once its work is done
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace binding set --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace binding set [WORKSPACE] [--pane PANE] --kind run|review|play --id ID [--step STEP] [--attempt N] [--focus TEXT] [--instructions PATH] [--artifacts PATH] [--pack NAME]... [--name NAME] [--json]

Bind a pane to a workflow run, a PR review or a library play.

When the agent in a bound pane starts a session (startup, /clear, resume or compact), session-event
reminds it of its subject, so it survives a lost context. Nothing is typed into the pane. A pane is
stored by its tmux pane id (%19) and only counts in the tmux session it was bound in. Setting a
binding replaces the whole earlier one, its packs included. This records the binding for real, in
bindings.json; there is no dry run.

Options:
    --name NAME                  Workspace name (default: the project detected from the current directory)
    --pane PANE                  Pane id (%19) or window.pane (0.1) of the workspace's own session; defaults to $TMUX_PANE
    --kind KIND                  run, review or play
    --id ID                      Run id, review id such as acme/api#835, or play/NAME
    --step STEP                  Step name
    --attempt N                  Step attempt, 1 or more
    --focus TEXT                 Review focus, e.g. security
    --instructions PATH          File holding the pane's instructions; stored as an absolute path
    --artifacts PATH             Directory holding the subject's artifacts; stored as an absolute path
    --pack NAME                  Library pack the agent is also reminded of (repeatable; replaces the stored list; see `workspace instructions --help`)
    --json                       Print one JSON action document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace binding set --kind play --id play/orchestrator    # from inside the agent's own pane: remind it of a play after a /clear
  workspace binding set my-app --pane %5 --kind run --id wr_01 --step implement --attempt 2    # bind the pane of a workflow run's second implement attempt
  workspace binding set my-app --pane 0.1 --kind review --id acme/api#835 --focus security    # bind a review pane by window.pane, with the focus the reviewer was given
  workspace binding set --pane %5 --kind play --id play/research --pack commits --pack notes    # also remind the agent of two packs, which replaces any packs stored before
  workspace binding set --pane %5 --kind run --id wr_01 --json    # for a script: the stored binding as one JSON action document
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace binding show --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace binding show [--pane %ID] [--json]

Print a pane's binding.

A binding ties a tmux pane to a workflow run, a PR review or a library play, so session-event can remind the agent in it of its subject.
It is marked stale when the pane is no longer in the tmux session and slot it was bound in; a stale binding is not announced.

Options:
    --pane PANE                  Pane id (%19); defaults to $TMUX_PANE, the pane the command runs in
    --json                       Print one JSON action document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace binding show    # from inside an agent's pane: what it is reminded of after a /clear
  workspace binding show --pane %5    # check a pane after a restore: is its binding stale?
  workspace binding show --pane %5 --json    # for a script: stale, packs and plays as fields; a pane with no binding exits 1 with not_bound
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace binding clear --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace binding clear [--pane %ID] [--json]

Remove a pane's binding.

A binding ties a tmux pane to a workflow run, a PR review or a library play, so session-event can remind the agent in it of its subject.
This removes the pane's entry from bindings.json for real; nothing is typed into the pane.

Options:
    --pane PANE                  Pane id (%19); defaults to $TMUX_PANE, the pane the command runs in
    --json                       Print one JSON action document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace binding clear    # from inside the agent's pane: stop reminding it once its work is done
  workspace binding clear --pane %5    # unbind another pane, e.g. one whose run was cancelled
  workspace binding clear --pane %5 --json    # for a script: the removed binding as one JSON action document; a pane with no binding exits 1 with not_bound
--- stderr
--- end

--- exit 0
--- stdout

--- exit 1
